theOneSlotRule.ruleText: On a turn, you can expend only one spell slot to cast a spell.
theOneSlotRule.source: 2024 Player's Handbook / official free rules, 'Casting Spells'
consequences: You CANNOT cast a slotted spell with your Action and another slotted spell with your Bonus Action on the same turn.
You CANNOT cast Divine Smite twice on one turn.
You CANNOT combine two Smite spells on a single hit.
You CANNOT use Action Surge (multiclass) to cast a second slotted spell.
Cantrips are unaffected - they expend no slot, so a slotted spell plus any number of cantrips is legal.
Features that let you cast a spell WITHOUT expending a slot are also unaffected.
theOneSlotRule.change2014: 2014's rule was different: casting a spell with a Bonus Action limited your Action to a cantrip. 2024 removed that and replaced it with the one-slot-per-turn restriction. Apps that still encode the 2014 rule will be wrong in both directions.

freeCastLoophole.summary: The restriction is on EXPENDING a slot, not on casting. A Paladin's free castings do not expend slots.
applies: Paladin's Smite (level 2): one free Divine Smite per Long Rest.
Faithful Steed (level 5): one free Find Steed per Long Rest.
Magic Initiate / Fey-Touched / Shadow-Touched style feats: one free casting per Long Rest.
freeCastLoophole.result: RAW, on one turn per Long Rest you may cast a slotted spell with your Action AND free-cast Divine Smite with your Bonus Action. Flag this to the DM before relying on it, but the rules text supports it.
freeCastLoophole.confidence: High on the rules text; confirm at your table.

concentration.onePerCharacter: You can concentrate on only one spell at a time. Casting another Concentration spell immediately ends the first.
concentration.saveOnDamage: Constitution saving throw, DC 10 or half the damage taken, whichever is higher.
endsWhen: You fail the Constitution save after taking damage
concentration.note2024: The Incapacitated condition now explicitly ends Concentration. This means Stunned, Paralyzed, Petrified and Unconscious all break Concentration automatically.

components.verbal: You must be able to speak. Being gagged, Silenced, or Incapacitated blocks it.
components.somatic: You need at least one free hand to gesture. A hand holding a Spellcasting Focus counts as free for this purpose.
components.material: You need a hand free to access the components. Components are not consumed unless the spell says so.
components.focusSubstitution: A Spellcasting Focus (a Holy Symbol, for a Paladin) or a component pouch replaces material components ONLY IF the component has no listed gold-piece cost AND is not consumed. Costed or consumed components must be owned and expended physically.
components.appRule: Track costed/consumed components as real inventory. A Paladin who cannot cast Revivify because no diamond was bought is a bug in the party's planning, and the app should catch it.

ritualCasting.rule: A spell with the Ritual tag can be cast as a Ritual: it takes 10 minutes longer and expends no spell slot. The caster must have it prepared.
ritualCasting.change2024: In 2014, ritual casting required a class feature or the Ritual Caster feat. In 2024 it is a universal rule tied to the spell. PALADINS CAN NOW RITUAL-CAST.

longCastingTimes: For a spell with a casting time of 1 minute or more, you must take the Magic action on each of your turns and maintain Concentration throughout. If Concentration breaks, the spell fails but the slot is NOT expended.
readiedSpells: You may Ready a spell whose casting time is an Action. The slot is spent when you Ready it, and you must concentrate on the held spell until the trigger fires.
higherLevelSlots: Casting with a higher-level slot makes the spell that level for that casting. Effects marked 'Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot' scale accordingly.
